What is HTML?:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages. It uses tags to structure content. HTML documents form the backbone of every website.

An HTML document starts with a DOCTYPE declaration, followed by <html>, <head>, and <body> elements.

Document Structure: Every HTML document has a standard structure. The <!DOCTYPE html> declaration defines the document type. The <html> element wraps all content. Inside <head> we put metadata. Inside <body> we put visible content.

Headings & Paragraphs: HTML provides six levels of headings (<h1> to <h6>) to structure content hierarchically. <h1> is most important, <h6> the least. Paragraphs use <p>. Use <br> for line breaks and <hr> for thematic breaks.

Text Formatting: Use <strong> for importance, <em> for emphasis, <mark> for highlighted text, <small> for fine print, <del> for deleted text, and <ins> for inserted text. Use <sub> for subscript and <sup> for superscript.
Comments & Attributes: HTML comments: <!-- comment -->. Attributes provide element metadata: id (unique), class (CSS class), style (inline CSS), title (tooltip). Use data-* attributes for custom data.

Links & Anchors: Links use the <a> tag with href. Use target="_blank" for new tabs. Links can target external pages, internal sections (#id), emails (mailto:), and phones (tel:).

Images: The <img> tag embeds images. Required attributes: src (path) and alt (accessibility text). Optional: width, height, loading="lazy". Wrap in <figure>/<figcaption> for captions.
Lists: Three list types: unordered <ul>, ordered <ol>, and description <dl>. List items use <li>. Nested lists go inside <li> elements.

Tables: Tables use <table>, <tr> (row), <th> (header), <td> (data). Group with <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>. Merge cells with colspan and rowspan.
Forms & Inputs: Forms collect user input. The <form> element wraps controls. Common input types: text, password, email, number, checkbox, radio, file, date. Always pair with <label>.

<form action="/submit" method="POST">
    <label for="name">Name:</label>
    <input type="text" id="name" name="name" required>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="subscribe"> Subscribe</label>
    <select name="country">
        <option value="">Select</option>
        <option value="us">USA</option>
    </select>
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
Block-Level vs Inline Elements: HTML elements are either block-level (start on a new line, take full width) or inline (flow within text). Common block: <div>, <p>, <h1>-<h6>, <section>. Common inline: <span>, <a>, <strong>, <img>. CSS display can change this behavior.

Semantic HTML: Semantic HTML uses meaningful tags: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer>. This improves accessibility, SEO, and code readability.

Audio & Video: Embed media with <audio> and <video>. Use <source> for multiple formats. The controls attribute shows playback UI. Use <track> for subtitles. Supported: MP3, MP4, WebM, OGG.

<audio controls>
    <source src="song.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="song.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
    Browser does not support audio.
</audio>

<video width="640" height="360" controls>
    <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track src="subtitles.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="en">
</video>
Iframes: The <iframe> tag embeds another HTML page. Use sandbox for security, loading="lazy" for deferred loading, and always set title for accessibility.

<iframe src="https://www.example.com" width="800" height="600" title="Example"></iframe>

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" title="YouTube" allowfullscreen sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"></iframe>
SVG Graphics: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is embeddable directly in HTML. Elements: <circle>, <rect>, <path>, <text>, <g>. SVG scales infinitely without quality loss.

<svg width="200" height="200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <rect x="10" y="10" width="180" height="180" rx="10" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="80" r="40" fill="#FF6B6B"/>
    <text x="100" y="160" text-anchor="middle" fill="white">SVG</text>
</svg>
Canvas: The <canvas> element provides a drawable region manipulated via JavaScript. Supports 2D graphics, charts, animations, and game rendering. Unlike SVG, canvas is pixel-based.

<canvas id="myCanvas" width="400" height="300"></canvas>
<script>
const c = document.getElementById("myCanvas");
const ctx = c.getContext("2d");
ctx.fillStyle = "#4A90D9";
ctx.fillRect(50, 50, 150, 100);
ctx.fillStyle = "white";
ctx.font = "20px Arial";
ctx.fillText("Canvas", 90, 110);
</script>
Data Attributes: Custom data-* attributes store extra info on elements. Access via JavaScript element.dataset. Useful for storing state or configuration without non-standard attributes.

Picture & Responsive Images: The <picture> element provides responsive images with multiple <source> elements using media queries. Works with srcset for resolution switching.
Embedded Content: Use <object> and <embed> for embedding PDFs, plugins, or legacy content. <param> passes parameters. Modern practice prefers native HTML or iframes.
MathML: MathML marks up mathematical notation using <math> and child elements like <mi>, <mo>, <mfrac>, <msqrt>. Natively supported in modern browsers.

Form Validation: HTML5 validation attributes: required (mandatory), minlength/maxlength (text length), min/max (range), pattern (regex). CSS pseudo-classes :valid/:invalid style states.

Interactive Elements: HTML5 interactive elements: <details>/<summary> for disclosure widgets, <dialog> for modals. These provide built-in interactivity without JavaScript.

Hidden Inputs & Form Security: Hidden inputs (<input type="hidden">) store data not visible to users. Use for CSRF tokens, session IDs, and form state. Security measures: validate server-side, use CSRF tokens, set proper enctype, never trust hidden values.

<form action="/checkout" method="POST">
    <!-- Hidden CSRF token -->
    <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="abc123def456">
    
    <!-- Hidden product data -->
    <input type="hidden" name="product_id" value="9876">
    <input type="hidden" name="price" value="29.99">

    <label>Quantity: <input type="number" name="qty" min="1" value="1"></label>
    <button type="submit">Buy Now</button>
</form>

Form Attributes Deep Dive: Advanced form attributes: novalidate skips validation, enctype="multipart/form-data" for files, form attribute lets inputs live outside <form>.

<form id="main-form" action="/api/submit" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data" novalidate>
    <input type="file" name="avatar">
</form>
<input type="email" form="main-form">
<input type="submit" form="main-form" value="Submit">

Web Storage: Web Storage API: localStorage (persists across sessions) and sessionStorage (cleared on tab close). Both store key-value pairs as strings. ~5MB per origin.
Geolocation API: Geolocation API accesses user location via navigator.geolocation. getCurrentPosition() for one-time, watchPosition() for tracking. Handle permission denial gracefully.
Drag & Drop API: Drag and Drop API: Set draggable="true" on elements. Events: dragstart, dragover, drop. Use dataTransfer to pass data between drag source and target.

Web Workers: Web Workers run JS in background threads. Communicate via postMessage() / onmessage. Cannot access DOM, window, or parent. Great for CPU-intensive tasks.
Server-Sent Events: Server-Sent Events (SSE) push updates from server to client over HTTP. Use EventSource to subscribe. Simpler than WebSockets for unidirectional data flow.
WebSockets: WebSockets provide full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection. Events: open, message, close, error. Ideal for real-time apps like chat and games.
Fetch API: Fetch API provides promise-based HTTP requests. fetch(url, options) returns a Response promise. Use response.json(), response.text(), or response.blob().
File API & Blobs: File API reads local files via <input type="file"> and FileReader. Blob represents binary data. Use URL.createObjectURL() for file previews.

<input type="file" id="fileInput" multiple accept="image/*">
<script>
document.getElementById("fileInput").onchange = function(e) {
    for (const file of e.target.files) {
        const reader = new FileReader();
        reader.onload = (ev) => {
            const img = document.createElement("img");
            img.src = ev.target.result;
            img.style.maxWidth = "200px";
            document.body.appendChild(img);
        };
        reader.readAsDataURL(file);
    }
};
</script>
IndexedDB: IndexedDB is a browser-based NoSQL database. Stores structured objects with indexes for fast queries. Asynchronous API. Use for complex client-side storage beyond localStorage.
History API: History API manipulates browser session history. pushState() adds entries, replaceState() modifies current. Listen for popstate events. Essential for SPAs.
Web Components: Web Components let you create reusable custom elements. Use customElements.define(), Shadow DOM for encapsulation, <template> for markup, and <slot> for composition.
Service Workers: Service Workers act as proxy between browser and network. Enable offline support, caching, push notifications, and background sync. They run in a separate thread and cannot access DOM.

Semantic Structure Deep Dive: Proper landmark elements: exactly one <main>, one <h1>. Use <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer> for page regions.
Microdata & Structured Data: Microdata adds machine-readable semantics via itemscope, itemtype, itemprop. Schema.org provides vocabulary. Enables rich search results like stars, prices, and recipes.

Performance Optimization: Optimize HTML delivery: use defer for scripts, rel="preload" for critical assets, rel="preconnect" for third-party origins, inline critical CSS. Reduce DOM size and render-blocking resources.

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preload" href="critical.css" as="style">
<script src="app.js" defer></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'">
<noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"></noscript>
Lazy Loading & Hints: Lazy loading defers off-screen resources. Use loading="lazy" on images/iframes. Resource hints: preload (critical), prefetch (future), preconnect (early connection).
WCAG Accessibility: WCAG principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust (POUR). Target WCAG 2.1 AA minimum. Use skip links, proper heading hierarchy, sufficient color contrast, keyboard navigation.

What is CSS?: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML. Rules consist of a selector and a declaration block with properties and values. Apply via inline, internal (<style>), or external (.css file).
Selectors: CSS selectors target elements: element (p), class (.my-class), id (#my-id), attribute ([type="text"]), universal (*). Combinators: descendant (div p), child (div > p), sibling (h2 + p).
Colors & Units: Color formats: named (red), hex (#FF5733), RGB (rgb(255, 87, 51)), RGBA (rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5)), HSL/HSLA. Units: px, em (relative to parent font), rem (relative to root), %, vw/vh, ch.
Typography: Typography properties: font-family, font-size, font-weight (100-900), font-style, text-align, text-decoration, text-transform, line-height, letter-spacing. Use web fonts via @font-face or Google Fonts.
Box Model: Every element is a box: content (inner), padding (around content), border (edge), margin (outside). Use box-sizing: border-box to include padding/border in width.
CSS Variables: CSS custom properties (variables) defined with --name, accessed with var(--name). They cascade and can be overridden, enabling easy theme systems.
Specificity & Cascade: CSS specificity determines which rule wins. Inline > ID > Class > Element. When equal, last rule wins. Use !important sparingly — it breaks the natural cascade.
Inheritance: Some CSS properties inherit from parent elements: color, font-family, line-height. Others like margin, padding, border do not. Control with inherit, initial, unset, revert.
Cascade Layers Intro: The @layer rule defines cascade layers. Styles in later layers override earlier ones regardless of specificity. Use to organize resets, base styles, components, and utilities in predictable order.
CSS Reset & Normalize: Browsers apply default styles inconsistently. CSS resets remove all defaults (margin: 0, padding: 0). Normalize.css preserves useful defaults while fixing cross-browser differences. Choose based on project needs.

Display Property: The display property controls rendering: block (full width, new line), inline (flows with text), inline-block (inline but accepts width/height), none (hidden, removed from flow). Modern: flex, grid.
Flexbox: Flexbox is a 1D layout model. Container: display: flex. Main axis: justify-content. Cross axis: align-items. Items wrap with flex-wrap, grow with flex-grow, order with order.
CSS Grid: CSS Grid is a 2D layout system. Define columns with grid-template-columns, rows with grid-template-rows. Use grid-area with named template areas for complex layouts.
Positioning: position values: static (default), relative (offset from normal), absolute (relative to positioned ancestor), fixed (relative to viewport), sticky (toggles between relative/fixed on scroll).
Responsive Design: Media queries adapt layouts to screen sizes. Use @media (min-width: ...) for mobile-first approach. Common breakpoints: 576px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 992px (desktop), 1200px (wide).
Backgrounds & Gradients: Background properties: background-color, background-image, background-size, background-position, background-repeat. Gradients: linear-gradient() and radial-gradient(). Multiple backgrounds can be layered.
Animations: CSS animations use @keyframes to define sequences. The animation shorthand: name, duration, timing function, delay, iteration count, direction, fill mode.
List Styling & Counters: Style lists with list-style-type, list-style-position, list-style-image. CSS counters (counter-reset, counter-increment) create numbered headings, table-of-contents, or custom list numbering.
Form Styling with CSS: Style form elements using CSS: inputs, textareas, selects, checkboxes, radio buttons, and buttons. Normalize browser defaults. Use :focus, :valid, :invalid, :disabled pseudo-classes for state styling.

Box Shadows: The box-shadow property adds shadows: offset-x offset-y blur-radius spread-radius color. Multiple shadows can be layered. Use inset for inner shadows.
Text Effects: Text styling: text-shadow for shadows, text-overflow for ellipsis, word-break for breaking long words, white-space for spacing control, text-wrap for wrapping behavior.
Filters & Blend Modes: CSS filter applies visual effects: blur(), brightness(), contrast(), grayscale(), sepia(), hue-rotate(), drop-shadow(). mix-blend-mode blends elements with their background.
Clip Path & Shapes: clip-path clips elements to a shape: circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), inset(). shape-outside makes text wrap around a shape.
Object Fit & Position: object-fit controls how replaced elements (images, videos) fit their container: fill, contain, cover, none, scale-down. object-position sets alignment within the box.
Overflow & Scroll: overflow controls content overflow: visible, hidden, scroll, auto. overflow-x/overflow-y for axis-specific. scroll-behavior: smooth for smooth scrolling. scroll-snap for snap points.
Cursor & Pointer Events: The cursor property changes the mouse cursor: pointer, grab, text, not-allowed, wait. pointer-events controls click/touch behavior: auto (default), none (disable), visiblePainted (SVG).
Resize & Object View: The resize property makes elements user-resizable: both, horizontal, vertical. field-sizing makes textareas/contenteditable auto-size. object-view-box crops replaced elements without changing the image.
Columns & Multi-Column: Multi-column layout with column-count, column-width, column-gap, column-rule. Content flows automatically between columns. Useful for text-heavy layouts like newspapers.

CSS Architecture (BEM): Scalable CSS methodologies: BEM (Block Element Modifier) uses naming like .block__element--modifier. Prevents conflicts and improves maintainability by enforcing naming conventions.
Preprocessors (Sass/SCSS): CSS preprocessors extend CSS with variables, nesting, mixins, functions. SCSS features: $variables, @mixin/@include, & parent selector, built-in functions for colors and math.
CSS Layers (@layer): The @layer rule controls cascade layer order. Later layers override earlier ones regardless of specificity. Useful for organizing resets, components, and utilities.
Container Queries: Container queries (@container) style elements based on container size rather than viewport. Define a containment context with container-type. Enables truly reusable components.
Nesting & @scope: CSS nesting (native) lets you nest selectors like SCSS. The @scope rule limits styles to a subtree, providing better encapsulation without Shadow DOM.
Logical Properties: Logical properties use flow-relative directions: margin-inline-start instead of margin-left, padding-block instead of padding-top/padding-bottom. Better for internationalization and RTL support.
CSS Functions: Powerful CSS functions: calc() for math, min()/max()/clamp() for responsive values, attr() for HTML attributes, url() for resources, var() for variables.
Content Visibility: content-visibility skips rendering of off-screen elements for performance. contain isolates layout/style/paint. content-visibility: auto automatically skips hidden content.
CSS Color Modern Functions: Modern CSS color functions: color-mix() blends colors, color() accesses wider gamuts (Display P3, sRGB), lch()/lab() for perceptually uniform colors, oklch()/oklab() for better gradients.
@property & Custom Properties Deep Dive: The @property rule defines typed CSS custom properties with initial values and inheritance control. Enables animation of custom properties, validation, and better developer ergonomics.
Container Query Units & Style Queries: Container query units: cqw (1% container width), cqh (1% height), cqi (1% inline size), cqb (1% block size), cqmin/cqmax. Style queries (@container style()) query computed style values.
View Transitions API: View Transitions animate between page states or navigations. Use @view-transition navigation rule, view-transition-name on elements, and ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements for custom animations.

CSS Methodologies: Beyond BEM: SMACSS (categorizes into base/layout/module/state/theme), ITCSS (layers by specificity), OOCSS (separates structure from skin, container from content). Choose what fits your project.
PostCSS & Autoprefixer: PostCSS is a tool for transforming CSS with JavaScript plugins. Autoprefixer automatically adds vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-, etc.). Other plugins enable future CSS syntax today.
Tailwind CSS & Utility-First: Utility-first CSS uses small, composable classes. Tailwind CSS provides .flex, .text-center, .p-4 etc. Encourages design consistency and reduces CSS file size. Trade-off: verbose HTML.

CSS Modules & Scoped Styles: CSS Modules generate locally scoped class names. Imported like JS modules. Class names are hashed at build time to avoid conflicts. Works well with component frameworks like React, Vue, Svelte.
CSS Grid Advanced: Advanced Grid: subgrid passes grid tracks to children. auto-fill/auto-fit for responsive grids without media queries. grid-auto-flow: dense fills gaps automatically.
Performance & Best Practices: CSS performance: minimize specificity chains, avoid expensive properties (box-shadow, border-radius), use will-change sparingly, avoid @import, reduce repaints/reflows, use GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity).
CSS Debugging & DevTools: Browser DevTools: inspect computed styles, trace specificity, toggle pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus), edit live CSS, view box model diagram, debug animations with timeline. Use outline to visualize elements.
Print & Accessibility Styles: Print stylesheets optimize pages for paper: hide nav/sidebars/ads, use page-break-* properties, ensure link URLs print. Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, forced-colors.
